passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: This Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations is intended to provide a reader of our financial statements with management’s perspective on our financial condition, liquidity, results of operations and certain other factors that may affect our future results. This information is intended to provide investors with an understanding of our past performance, current financial condition and outlook for the future and should be read in conjunction with Item 8 of Part II of this report. Introduction On October 1, 2024, we completed the Southwestern Merger, creating a premier energy company that we believe is underpinned by a leading natural gas portfolio adjacent to the highest demand markets, premium inventory, a resilient financial foundation and an investment grade balance sheet. We believe that this new company is uniquely positioned to deliver affordable, lower-carbon energy to meet growing domestic and international demand while creating sustainable value for stakeholders. In conjunction with the closing of the Southwestern Merger, Chesapeake Energy Corporation changed its name to Expand Energy Corporation. Expand Energy is the largest independent natural gas producer in the U.S., based on net daily production, and is focused on responsibly developing an abundant supply of natural gas, oil and NGL to expand energy access for all. Our operations are located in Louisiana and Texas in the Haynesville and Bossier Shales (“Haynesville”), in Pennsylvania in the Marcellus Shale (“Northeast Appalachia”) and in West Virginia and Ohio in the Marcellus and Utica Shales (“Southwest Appalachia”). Our strategy is to create resilient shareholder value through the responsible development of our significant resource plays while continuing to be a leading provider of natural gas to growing markets. We continue to focus on improving margins through operating efficiencies, marketing and commercial efforts and financial discipline and improving our safety and sustainability performance. To accomplish these goals, we plan to allocate our human resources and capital expenditures to projects we believe offer the highest cash return on capital invested, to deploy leading drilling and completion technology throughout our portfolio, and to take advantage of acquisition and divestiture opportunities to strengthen our portfolio. We also intend to continue to invest in projects designed to reduce the environmental impact of our production activities. Additionally, we aim to be conscientious in our efforts and how they will shape our approach to sustainability for the future and have established the following goals: • Net zero (Scope 1 and 2) greenhouse gas emissions by 2035. • Maintain 100% responsibly sourced gas (RSG) certification across our portfolio. 54 TABLE OF CONTENTS Recent and Significant Developments Southwestern Merger On October 1, 2024, we completed the Southwestern Merger and issued approximately 95.7 million shares of our common stock to Southwestern’s shareholders in connection with the Merger Agreement. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: There are numerous factors that affect our business and results of operations, many of which are beyond our control. The following is a description of factors that we consider to be material and that might cause our future results to differ materially from those currently expected. The risks described below are not the only risks facing our company. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our business operations. If any of these risks actually occur, our business, financial position, results of operations, cash flows, reserves and/or our ability to pay our debts and other liabilities could suffer, the trading price and liquidity of our securities could decline and you may lose all or part of your investment in our securities. Risks Related to Operating our Business Natural gas, oil and NGL prices fluctuate widely, and lower prices for an extended period of time are likely to have a material adverse effect on our business. Our revenues, results of operations, profitability, liquidity, leverage ratio and ability to grow and invest in capital expenditures depend primarily upon the prices we receive for the natural gas, oil and NGL we sell. We incur substantial expenditures to replace reserves, sustain production and fund our business plans. Low natural gas, oil and NGL prices can negatively affect the amount of cash available for capital expenditures, debt service and debt repayment and our ability to borrow money or raise additional capital and, as a result, could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations, cash flows and reserves. In addition, periods of low natural gas and oil prices may result in a reduction of the carrying value of our natural gas and oil properties due to recognizing impairments in proved and unproved properties. Volatility in natural gas, oil and NGL prices may result from factors that are beyond our control, including: • domestic and worldwide supplies of natural gas, oil and NGL, including U.S. inventories of natural gas and oil reserves; • weather conditions; • changes in the level of consumer and industrial demand, including impacts from global or national health events and concerns; • the price and availability of alternative fuels; • technological advances affecting energy consumption; • the nature and extent of domestic and international conservation and sustainability initiatives; • the availability, proximity and capacity of pipelines, other transportation facilities and processing facilities; • the level and effect of trading in commodity futures markets, including by commodity price speculators and others; • U.S. exports of natural gas, oil, liquefied natural gas and NGL; • the price and level of foreign imports; • changes in U.S. trade relations and policies; • the nature and extent of domestic and foreign governmental regulations and taxes; • the ability of the members of OPEC+ and others to agree to and maintain oil price and production controls; • increased use of competing energy products, including alternative energy sources; • political instability or armed conflict in natural gas and oil prod

credit_strengths.text: Scale and asset quality improved materially after the Southwestern Merger, leaving Expand Energy the largest independent U.S. natural gas producer with Haynesville and Appalachia inventory. Operating margin sits above the sector median, and operating income swung back to a solid profit after the prior year loss, supporting cash generation through the cycle.

Leverage is conservative for the sector: gross leverage sits well below the sector median and fell sharply year over year as debt was repaid and EBITDA recovered. Net leverage on a cash-and-investments basis also sits below the sector median and comfortably inside the next risk-band boundary, leaving meaningful headroom against an EBITDA decline.

key_risks.text: Cash flow and debt service depend primarily on natural gas, oil and NGL prices, which the risk factors describe as widely fluctuating and beyond management control. Extended low prices would pressure revenues, leverage and the ability to fund capital spending and debt repayment, and could trigger property impairments, a concrete exposure for a pure-play gas producer.

The debt note shows a concentrated maturity ladder: nothing due in the near years, but a large slug of senior notes falls due in the fourth year and further amounts in the fifth year and thereafter. Refinancing that cluster depends on market access and rates at the time, and the credit facility was undrawn at year end.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is strong and far above the sector median, with operating income covering gross interest expense many times over; coverage also improved sharply year over year. EBITDA-based coverage similarly exceeds the sector median, indicating ample room to absorb higher borrowing costs or a moderate earnings setback.

Operating cash flow comfortably exceeds capital expenditure plus shareholder distributions, and free cash flow covers dividends and buybacks more than twice over. Free cash flow to debt is above the sector median and improved dramatically year over year, so internally generated cash funds both the capital programme and returns.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, driven by low leverage and strong cash-flow-to-debt, with headroom to the next risk band on both measures. Liquidity is adequate rather than abundant: the current ratio is marginally above one but below the sector median, and cash balances are modest relative to debt, so refinancing access matters.

Our judgement is a stable, investment-grade-like profile: low leverage, high coverage and self-funding capital spending support the notes, while commodity price cyclicality and the later-year maturity cluster are the main sensitivities. A sustained gas price slump, not leverage today, is the realistic path to deterioration.

credit_strengths.text: 完成Southwestern合併後，規模與資產質量顯著改善，使Expand Energy成為美國最大的獨立天然氣生產商，擁有Haynesville與Appalachia庫存。營業利潤率高於行業中位數，且營業利潤在上一年的虧損後回升至穩健盈利，支撐整個週期的現金生成。
槓桿對該行業而言屬保守：總槓桿遠低於行業中位數，並隨債務償還及EBITDA回升而同比大幅下降。以現金及投資為基礎的淨槓桿亦低於行業中位數，並穩妥地處於下一個風險區間邊界之內，對EBITDA下降留有充裕緩衝。

key_risks.text: 現金流與償債能力主要取決於天然氣、石油及NGL價格，風險因素將其描述為大幅波動且超出管理層控制。長期低價將對收入、槓桿以及為資本開支和債務償還提供資金的能力構成壓力，並可能觸發資產減值，這對純天然氣生產商而言是具體的風險敞口。
債務附註顯示到期結構集中：近幾年無到期，但第四年有一大筆優先票據到期，第五年及之後還有進一步金額。該集中到期的再融資取決於當時的市場準入與利率，而信貸額度於年末未提取。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率強勁且遠高於行業中位數，營業利潤覆蓋總利息支出的倍數甚高；覆蓋率亦同比大幅改善。以EBITDA為基礎的覆蓋率同樣超過行業中位數，表明有充足空間吸收更高的借貸成本或適度的盈利挫折。
經營現金流穩健超過資本開支加股東分派，自由現金流覆蓋股息及回購超過兩倍。自由現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數並同比大幅改善，因此內部產生的現金可同時為資本計劃及回報提供資金。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為極低，受低槓桿及強勁的現金流對債務比率驅動，兩項指標對下一個風險區間均有緩衝。流動性屬充足而非充裕：流動比率略高於一但低於行業中位數，且現金餘額相對債務而言適度，因此再融資渠道至關重要。
我們的判斷為穩定、類投資級別的狀況：低槓桿、高覆蓋率及自我融資的資本開支支撐票據，而商品價格週期性及後期到期集中為主要敏感因素。持續的天然氣價格下滑，而非當前的槓桿，才是惡化的現實路徑。
